name: Alfred's burh system
summary: After Alfred the Great's victory at the Battle of Edington (878) and the Treaty of Wedmore that created the Danelaw, Alfred reorganizes Wessex's defense around a systematic network of fortified towns (burhs). Approximately 33 burhs are established, spaced so no point in Wessex is more than 20 miles from a fortification. Each burh requires a garrison proportional to its defensive perimeter. The Burghal Hidage (document c.919) records the system. Combined with a reformed naval force and the reconstituted fyrd, the burh system transforms Wessex from a reactive to a proactive defender against Danish raids.

_quarry.structural_significance: Creates the defensive infrastructure that enables the reconquest of the Danelaw; establishes urban centers that become the economic foundation of medieval England; models a new theory of territorial defense
